reason: Both conversations refuse the DIY regas clearly, but Conversation 2 reaches a firm and useful conclusion: it is probably a sealed-system failure, R600a is flammable, a gas top-up won't work, and replacement is likely more economical than repair. That suits a 9-year-old, out-of-warranty fridge and a customer who wants the cheapest option. Conversation 1 wanders through contradictory causes (defrost, condenser, seals) and repeats defrost advice. It ends by telling the customer to keep the doors shut for 24 hours and 'let it recover', which doesn't fit a leak, and it never addresses cost or replacement. Conversation 2 has weaknesses: it wrongly blames compressor wear, suggests an unnecessary 24-hour defrost, and ignores the knife-defrosting clue. Conversation 1 does tie the oily mark to a leak, but its overall guidance is less coherent and less helpful.
